cards.loText: Describe the terms of a collateral agreement and features of a credit support annex (CSA) within the ISDA Master Agreement including threshold, initial margin, minimum transfer amount and rounding, haircuts, credit quality, and credit support amount.
cards.statement: The purpose of a credit support annex is to provide a mechanism for netting and settlement of trades.
cards.explanation: Netting and settlement come from the ISDA Master Agreement. The CSA deals with collateral.
cards.originalText: To provide a mechanism for netting and settlement of trades.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the terms of a collateral agreement and features of a credit support annex (CSA) within the ISDA Master Agreement including threshold, initial margin, minimum transfer amount and rounding, haircuts, credit quality, and credit support amount.
cards.statement: The purpose of a credit support annex is to ensure that all derivative contracts are honored by both parties.
cards.explanation: A CSA does not guarantee performance. It only provides collateral support that mitigates counterparty credit risk.
cards.originalText: To ensure that all derivative contracts are honored by both parties involved.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the terms of a collateral agreement and features of a credit support annex (CSA) within the ISDA Master Agreement including threshold, initial margin, minimum transfer amount and rounding, haircuts, credit quality, and credit support amount.
cards.statement: A credit support annex specifies the collateral terms, including events that trigger changes in collateral requirements.
cards.explanation: A CSA is a flexible, negotiated agreement that sets the collateral terms, including changes triggered by events such as a rating downgrade.
cards.originalText: It specifies the collateral terms, including events that trigger changes in collateral requirements.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the terms of a collateral agreement and features of a credit support annex (CSA) within the ISDA Master Agreement including threshold, initial margin, minimum transfer amount and rounding, haircuts, credit quality, and credit support amount.
cards.statement: A credit support annex mandates a fixed collateral amount for the duration of all derivative contracts.
cards.explanation: Collateral is recalculated regularly as the portfolio value changes. It is not fixed.
cards.originalText: It mandates a fixed collateral amount for the duration of all derivative contracts.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the terms of a collateral agreement and features of a credit support annex (CSA) within the ISDA Master Agreement including threshold, initial margin, minimum transfer amount and rounding, haircuts, credit quality, and credit support amount.
cards.statement: A credit support annex requires collateral to be posted exclusively in the form of government securities.
cards.explanation: Eligible collateral is negotiated, and cash is the most common form. Various securities can also be eligible.
cards.originalText: It requires collateral to be posted exclusively in the form of government securities.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the terms of a collateral agreement and features of a credit support annex (CSA) within the ISDA Master Agreement including threshold, initial margin, minimum transfer amount and rounding, haircuts, credit quality, and credit support amount.
cards.statement: A credit support annex requires the same threshold to apply to both parties regardless of their credit quality.
cards.explanation: Thresholds can differ by party and can be linked to credit quality, so they may be asymmetric.
cards.originalText: It requires the same threshold to apply to both parties regardless of their credit quality.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the terms of a collateral agreement and features of a credit support annex (CSA) within the ISDA Master Agreement including threshold, initial margin, minimum transfer amount and rounding, haircuts, credit quality, and credit support amount.
cards.statement: Collateral with higher price volatility, ceteris paribus, is assigned a higher haircut.
cards.explanation: Haircuts are driven by the volatility and liquidity of the collateral, so more volatile collateral gets a larger haircut.
cards.originalText: Collateral with higher price volatility, ceteris paribus, will be assigned a higher haircut

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the terms of a collateral agreement and features of a credit support annex (CSA) within the ISDA Master Agreement including threshold, initial margin, minimum transfer amount and rounding, haircuts, credit quality, and credit support amount.
cards.statement: A party that has already posted an independent amount (initial margin) can apply it against a variation margin call, so that it needs to deliver only the remainder.
cards.explanation: The independent amount is overcollateralisation held separately and is not netted against the variation margin call. The party must still deliver the full variation margin.
cards.originalText: If FundCorp has already posted an Independent Amount (IA) of \$60,000, then FundCorp can apply the IA and meet the margin call with only \$40,000

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the terms of a collateral agreement and features of a credit support annex (CSA) within the ISDA Master Agreement including threshold, initial margin, minimum transfer amount and rounding, haircuts, credit quality, and credit support amount.
cards.statement: A CSA is appended within an ISDA Master Agreement and permits the counterparties to mitigate their credit risk by agreeing to various collateral posting arrangements.
cards.explanation: The CSA is an annex to the ISDA Master Agreement that provides for collateral posting.
cards.originalText: A CSA is appended within an ISDA Master Agreement and permits the counterparties to mitigate their credit risk by agreeing to various collateral posting

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the terms of a collateral agreement and features of a credit support annex (CSA) within the ISDA Master Agreement including threshold, initial margin, minimum transfer amount and rounding, haircuts, credit quality, and credit support amount.
cards.statement: A CSA is critically defined by key parameters, including the threshold, the independent amount and the minimum transfer amount.
cards.explanation: Threshold, independent amount (initial margin) and minimum transfer amount are key CSA parameters.
cards.originalText: A CSA is critically defined by key parameters, including threshold, independent amount, and minimum transfer amount

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the terms of a collateral agreement and features of a credit support annex (CSA) within the ISDA Master Agreement including threshold, initial margin, minimum transfer amount and rounding, haircuts, credit quality, and credit support amount.
cards.statement: In some trading relationships CSAs are not used, because one or both parties cannot commit to collateral posting.
cards.explanation: Entities that cannot post collateral, such as many corporates, often have no CSA.
cards.originalText: In some trading relationships, CSAs are not used because one or both parties cannot commit to collateral posting

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the terms of a collateral agreement and features of a credit support annex (CSA) within the ISDA Master Agreement including threshold, initial margin, minimum transfer amount and rounding, haircuts, credit quality, and credit support amount.
cards.statement: If a counterparty employs a credit value adjustment (CVA), then a CSA gives no benefit and is not necessary.
cards.explanation: CVA prices the expected loss from counterparty risk, while a CSA reduces the exposure itself, and so reduces the CVA charge. The two complement each other.
cards.originalText: If a counterparty employs a credit value adjustment (CVA), then a CSA gives no benefit and is not necessary (a CSA would be redundant with CVA)

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the terms of a collateral agreement and features of a credit support annex (CSA) within the ISDA Master Agreement including threshold, initial margin, minimum transfer amount and rounding, haircuts, credit quality, and credit support amount.
cards.statement: ISDA documentation has helped standardize collateral management.
cards.explanation: Collateral management moved from no legal standards to highly standardized practice through ISDA documentation introduced in 1994.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the terms of a collateral agreement and features of a credit support annex (CSA) within the ISDA Master Agreement including threshold, initial margin, minimum transfer amount and rounding, haircuts, credit quality, and credit support amount.
cards.statement: CSAs must define all collateralization parameters in order to work as intended.
cards.explanation: A CSA must define every collateralization parameter and account for the relevant scenarios in order to work as intended.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the terms of a collateral agreement and features of a credit support annex (CSA) within the ISDA Master Agreement including threshold, initial margin, minimum transfer amount and rounding, haircuts, credit quality, and credit support amount.
cards.statement: CSAs are incorporated into an ISDA Master Agreement.
cards.explanation: A CSA is an annex incorporated into the ISDA Master Agreement, not a separate stand-alone agreement.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the terms of a collateral agreement and features of a credit support annex (CSA) within the ISDA Master Agreement including threshold, initial margin, minimum transfer amount and rounding, haircuts, credit quality, and credit support amount.
cards.statement: Compared to the ISDA Master Agreement, CSAs were first to establish collateral standards.
cards.explanation: The CSA is an annex to the ISDA Master Agreement, so the ISDA framework came first and the CSA did not precede it as a standard-setter.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the terms of a collateral agreement and features of a credit support annex (CSA) within the ISDA Master Agreement including threshold, initial margin, minimum transfer amount and rounding, haircuts, credit quality, and credit support amount.
cards.statement: Funding and capital costs, central clearing and bilateral margin requirements are pushing collateral thresholds increasingly toward zero.
cards.explanation: These pressures remove the benefit of leaving exposure uncollateralised, so thresholds are increasingly zero. Two-way CSAs with zero thresholds are standard between financial counterparties.
cards.originalText: Thresholds are increasingly set to zero

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the terms of a collateral agreement and features of a credit support annex (CSA) within the ISDA Master Agreement including threshold, initial margin, minimum transfer amount and rounding, haircuts, credit quality, and credit support amount.
cards.statement: Funding and capital costs, central clearing and bilateral margin requirements are pushing collateral thresholds increasingly toward infinity.
cards.explanation: An infinite threshold means a party never posts margin, as in a one-way CSA. That is the opposite of the trend toward more margining.
cards.originalText: Thresholds are increasingly set to infinity
cards.correction: Funding and capital costs, central clearing and bilateral margin requirements are pushing collateral thresholds increasingly toward zero.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the terms of a collateral agreement and features of a credit support annex (CSA) within the ISDA Master Agreement including threshold, initial margin, minimum transfer amount and rounding, haircuts, credit quality, and credit support amount.
cards.statement: Collateral thresholds are typically set equal to the initial margin.
cards.explanation: Thresholds and initial margin work in opposite directions, so they are not seen together. Where initial margin is present, the threshold is typically zero.
cards.originalText: Thresholds are typically set equal to the initial margin

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the terms of a collateral agreement and features of a credit support annex (CSA) within the ISDA Master Agreement including threshold, initial margin, minimum transfer amount and rounding, haircuts, credit quality, and credit support amount.
cards.statement: Counterparties agree to a non-zero (higher) threshold in a CSA mainly to reduce the operational workload and liquidity cost of margining, accepting some uncollateralised exposure.
cards.explanation: A higher threshold means fewer and smaller margin calls, trading some risk mitigation for lower operational and liquidity costs.
cards.originalText: To reduce the operational workload and liquidity cost of margining, accepting some uncollateralised exposure

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the terms of a collateral agreement and features of a credit support annex (CSA) within the ISDA Master Agreement including threshold, initial margin, minimum transfer amount and rounding, haircuts, credit quality, and credit support amount.
cards.statement: Counterparties agree to a non-zero (higher) threshold in a CSA to eliminate counterparty credit exposure entirely.
cards.explanation: A higher threshold leaves more exposure uncollateralised, so it cannot eliminate counterparty credit exposure.
cards.originalText: To eliminate counterparty credit exposure entirely

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the terms of a collateral agreement and features of a credit support annex (CSA) within the ISDA Master Agreement including threshold, initial margin, minimum transfer amount and rounding, haircuts, credit quality, and credit support amount.
cards.statement: Counterparties agree to a non-zero (higher) threshold in a CSA to increase the amount of collateral held against the current exposure.
cards.explanation: A higher threshold reduces the collateral held, because margin is called only on exposure above it. Initial margin is what increases collateral.
cards.originalText: To increase the amount of collateral held against the current exposure

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the terms of a collateral agreement and features of a credit support annex (CSA) within the ISDA Master Agreement including threshold, initial margin, minimum transfer amount and rounding, haircuts, credit quality, and credit support amount.
cards.statement: Under the regulatory margin requirements for non-centrally cleared derivatives, the initial margin amounts posted by the two parties may be netted against each other, so that only the net amount is exchanged.
cards.explanation: Initial margin is exchanged by both parties on a gross basis. Each party posts its own amount and the two amounts cannot be offset.
cards.originalText: Initial margin amounts posted by the two parties may be netted against each other, so that only the net amount is exchanged.
cards.correction: Under the regulatory margin requirements for non-centrally cleared derivatives, the initial margin amounts posted by the two parties may not be netted against each other, so the gross amounts are exchanged.

changes.from: only the net amount is exchanged

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the terms of a collateral agreement and features of a credit support annex (CSA) within the ISDA Master Agreement including threshold, initial margin, minimum transfer amount and rounding, haircuts, credit quality, and credit support amount.
cards.statement: Under the regulatory margin requirements for non-centrally cleared derivatives, variation margin must be exchanged regularly (for example daily) with a zero threshold.
cards.explanation: Variation margin is exchanged regularly and in full, without a threshold, unlike the thresholds common in ordinary CSAs.
cards.originalText: Variation margin must be exchanged regularly (for example daily) with a zero threshold.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the terms of a collateral agreement and features of a credit support annex (CSA) within the ISDA Master Agreement including threshold, initial margin, minimum transfer amount and rounding, haircuts, credit quality, and credit support amount.
cards.statement: Under the regulatory margin requirements for non-centrally cleared derivatives, initial margin may be calculated using validated internal models or regulatory tables, based on an extreme but plausible move over a 10-day horizon at a 99% confidence level.
cards.explanation: Initial margin is calibrated to an extreme but plausible move over 10 days at 99% confidence, using either validated models or regulatory tables.
cards.originalText: Initial margin may be calculated using validated internal models or regulatory tables, based on an extreme but plausible move over a 10‑day horizon at a 99% confidence level.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the process for the reconciliation of collateral disputes.
cards.statement: In a collateral valuation dispute, if the disputed amount is under an acceptable level stated in the collateral agreement, the counterparties may "split the difference"; otherwise, the cause of the difference must be found.
cards.explanation: Splitting the difference is a shortcut reserved for small differences. Larger disputes require identifying the root cause and, if unresolved, obtaining market-maker quotes.
cards.originalText: If the disputed amount is under an acceptable level stated in the collateral agreement, the counterparties may “split the difference”; otherwise, the cause of the difference must be found.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the process for the reconciliation of collateral disputes.
cards.statement: In a collateral valuation dispute, if the disputed amount is higher than an acceptable level stated in the collateral agreement, the counterparties may "split the difference".
cards.explanation: Splitting is for amounts below the acceptable level, not above it. Larger differences require finding the cause.
cards.originalText: If the disputed amount is higher than an acceptable level stated in the collateral agreement, the counterparties may “split the difference.”
cards.correction: In a collateral valuation dispute, if the disputed amount is lower than an acceptable level stated in the collateral agreement, the counterparties may "split the difference".

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the process for the reconciliation of collateral disputes.
cards.statement: In a collateral valuation dispute, if the disputed amount is under an acceptable level stated in the collateral agreement, the parties should ignore it.
cards.explanation: Small differences are not ignored. They are typically settled by splitting the difference.
cards.originalText: If the disputed amount is under an acceptable level stated in the collateral agreement, the parties should ignore it; otherwise, the cause of the difference must be found.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the process for the reconciliation of collateral disputes.
cards.statement: In reconciling a collateral dispute, the disputing party notifies the counterparty of its intent to dispute by the end of the day following the collateral call, transfers all undisputed amounts, and identifies the reason for the dispute.
cards.explanation: These are the first two steps of the standard process. Quotes from market makers are requested only if the dispute remains unresolved.
cards.originalText: Notify the counterparty of the intent to dispute by the end of the day following the collateral call, transfer all undisputed amounts, and identify the reason for the dispute.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the process for the reconciliation of collateral disputes.
cards.statement: In reconciling a collateral dispute, the standard first step is to immediately request quotes from several market makers for the mark-to-market value of the disputed trades.
cards.explanation: Market-maker quotes are the last step, used only for disputes that remain unresolved after the cause has been investigated.
cards.originalText: Immediately request quotes from several market makers for the MtM value of the disputed trades and temporarily exclude the problematic assets from collateral calls.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the process for the reconciliation of collateral disputes.
cards.statement: In reconciling a collateral dispute, the parties should split the difference on the disputed amount regardless of its size.
cards.explanation: Splitting the difference is acceptable only when the difference is small. Larger differences stay uncollateralised until the cause is found and resolved.
cards.originalText: Split the difference on the disputed amount regardless of its size to ensure a quick resolution and preserve the relationship.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the process for the reconciliation of collateral disputes.
cards.statement: To resolve a collateral dispute that stems from different market data and closing times, the parties should review both valuation methodologies, market data sources and market closing times used for the disputed trades to identify the cause.
cards.explanation: Market data and market close time are recognised sources of disputes. Standard practice is to transfer undisputed amounts and identify the reason for the dispute.
cards.originalText: Review both parties’ valuation methodologies, market data sources and the market closing times used for the disputed trades to identify the cause.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the process for the reconciliation of collateral disputes.
cards.statement: As a step in reconciling a collateral dispute, the disputing party notifies its counterparty (or the third-party valuation agent) that it disputes the exposure or collateral calculation.
cards.explanation: Notification of the dispute is the first step of the process.
cards.originalText: The disputing party notifies its counterparty (or the third‑party valuation agent) that it disputes the exposure or collateral calculation.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the process for the reconciliation of collateral disputes.
cards.statement: As a step in reconciling a collateral dispute, the disputing party identifies the reason for the dispute and transfers the undisputed amount, and the parties attempt to resolve the dispute within a resolution time.
cards.explanation: Transferring the undisputed amount and diagnosing the cause is the second step.
cards.originalText: The disputing party identifies the reason for the dispute and transfers the undisputed amount, and the parties attempt to resolve the dispute within a resolution time.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the process for the reconciliation of collateral disputes.
cards.statement: If the parties fail to resolve a collateral dispute within the resolution time, they obtain mark-to-market quotations from several market makers for the disputed components.
cards.explanation: Quotes from several market makers are the final step for unresolved disputes.
cards.originalText: If the parties fail to resolve the dispute within the resolution time, they obtain MtM quotations from several market makers for the disputed components.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the process for the reconciliation of collateral disputes.
cards.statement: In reconciling a collateral dispute, both parties post collateral for the full amount of any disputed exposure, even if this means mutual overcollateralization.
cards.explanation: Only undisputed amounts are transferred. The disputed exposure remains partly uncollateralised until the cause is traced and corrected.
cards.originalText: Both parties post collateral for the full amount of any disputed exposure, even if this means mutual overcollateralization, so that neither counterparty is partially exposed during the dispute.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the process for the reconciliation of collateral disputes.
cards.statement: Reconciling portfolios and valuations regularly, for example daily, and considering practice reconciliations before trading, reduces the chance of collateral disputes.
cards.explanation: Frequent reconciliation aligns the parties' trade populations, valuations and margin requirements before a call is made, which prevents disputes rather than settling them.
cards.originalText: Reconcile portfolios and valuations regularly, for example daily, and consider practice reconciliations before trading.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the process for the reconciliation of collateral disputes.
cards.statement: Naming both counterparties as valuation agents, so that each can call for collateral on its own valuation, reduces the chance of collateral disputes.
cards.explanation: Two valuation agents are used only when the counterparties are similar in size, and each calling on its own numbers can create disputes and processing delays.
cards.originalText: Name both parties as valuation agents so each can call for collateral on its own valuation.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the features of a collateralization agreement.
cards.statement: The valuation agent is the party calling for delivery or return of collateral and so must handle all calculations: credit exposure, market value of posted collateral, uncollateralized exposure, and the delivery or return amount.
cards.explanation: This is the standard list of valuation agent duties.
cards.originalText: The valuation agent is the party calling for delivery or return of collateral and thus must handle all calculations, i.e., calculation of credit exposure, market value of posted collateral, uncollateralized exposure, and the delivery or return amount

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the features of a collateralization agreement.
cards.statement: The threshold represents an amount of uncollateralized exposure: if an exposure is above the threshold, only the incremental exposure will be collateralized.
cards.explanation: Exposure below the threshold is uncollateralised, and only the excess above it is collateralised.
cards.originalText: The threshold represents an amount of uncollateralized exposure: if an exposure is above the threshold, only the incremental exposure will be collateralized

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the features of a collateralization agreement.
cards.statement: An independent amount is effectively a negative threshold and is typically held as a cushion against gap risk, the risk that a transaction's market value may gap substantially and quickly.
cards.explanation: The independent amount (initial margin) works in the opposite direction to the threshold and cushions gap risk.
cards.originalText: An independent amount is effectively a negative threshold and is typically held as a cushion against ”gap risk”, i.e., the risk that a transaction’s market value may gap substantially and quickly

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the features of a collateralization agreement.
cards.statement: A counterparty that posts a dividend-paying asset as collateral forfeits all dividends, because the receiver immediately becomes the economic owner of the collateral.
cards.explanation: The collateral receiver is only a temporary holder and must pass dividends and coupons through to the giver. The giver keeps the economic benefits.
cards.originalText: A counterparty who posts a dividend‑paying asset as collateral (i.e., the ”giver” of collateral) forfeits all dividends as the receiver immediately becomes the economic owner of the collateral

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the features of a collateralization agreement.
cards.statement: In a bilateral collateral agreement, a party with positive mark-to-market calls for collateral from its counterparty, and a party with negative mark-to-market has its counterparty call for collateral from it.
cards.explanation: Collateral flows from the party with negative MtM to the party with positive MtM, which is the party exposed to default.
cards.originalText: If its MtM is positive it calls for collateral from the counterparty, and if its MtM is negative the counterparty calls for collateral from it.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the features of a collateralization agreement.
cards.statement: In a bilateral collateral agreement, a party with positive mark-to-market posts collateral, and a party with negative mark-to-market calls for collateral.
cards.explanation: The flow is reversed: the party in the money is the one exposed to default and calls for collateral, while the party with negative MtM posts it.
cards.originalText: If its MtM is positive it posts collateral, and if its MtM is negative it calls for collateral.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the features of a collateralization agreement.
cards.statement: Some smaller institutions prefer a longer margin call frequency because it gives them more time to meet operational and funding requirements.
cards.explanation: A longer frequency reduces the operational and funding burden for institutions with limited capacity, at the cost of more uncollateralised exposure between calls.
cards.originalText: a longer frequency gives them more time to meet operational and funding requirements.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the features of a collateralization agreement.
cards.statement: A longer margin call frequency removes the counterparty's uncollateralized exposure between calls.
cards.explanation: A longer frequency increases the uncollateralised exposure between calls.
cards.originalText: a longer frequency removes the counterparty’s uncollateralized exposure between calls.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the features of a collateralization agreement.
cards.statement: Typical collateralization agreements link thresholds and initial margins to counterparty credit rating, use tiered haircuts reflecting collateral riskiness, and pay interest on cash collateral at the overnight market rate.
cards.explanation: Lower-rated counterparties get lower thresholds and larger initial margins, haircuts rise with collateral riskiness, and cash collateral earns the overnight rate.
cards.originalText: Thresholds and initial margins linked to counterparty credit rating, tiered haircuts reflecting collateral riskiness, and interest on cash collateral at the overnight market rate.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the features of a collateralization agreement.
cards.statement: Sound haircut practice assigns higher haircuts to riskier assets such as equities and commodities, and low or zero haircuts to cash and high-quality government bonds.
cards.explanation: Haircuts should scale with the collateral's volatility, liquidity and default risk.
cards.originalText: Higher haircuts for riskier assets such as equities and commodities, and low or zero haircuts for cash and high‑quality government bonds.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the features of a collateralization agreement.
cards.statement: Applying a uniform 5% haircut across cash, government bonds and equities is consistent with sound haircut practice.
cards.explanation: A uniform haircut penalises cash needlessly and understates the risk of equities. Haircuts should scale with the riskiness of the collateral.
cards.originalText: A uniform 5% haircut across cash, government bonds and equities to simplify calculation.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the features of a collateralization agreement.
cards.statement: Applying no haircuts at all is consistent with sound haircut practice, because it encourages counterparties to post collateral.
cards.explanation: Without haircuts the receiver is exposed to declines in the value of the collateral.
cards.originalText: No haircuts at all, to encourage counterparties to post collateral.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the features of a collateralization agreement.
cards.statement: Collateral agreements typically tier the minimum transfer amount by credit rating, with higher MTAs for higher-rated counterparties and lower MTAs for weaker ones.
cards.explanation: A larger MTA means more uncollateralised exposure, which is tolerable for strong credits. Weaker counterparties get lower MTAs to tighten mitigation where risk is greatest.
cards.originalText: Tier the MTA by credit rating, with higher MTAs for higher‑rated counterparties and lower MTAs for weaker ones.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the features of a collateralization agreement.
cards.statement: Collateral agreements typically tier the minimum transfer amount by credit rating, with higher MTAs for lower-rated counterparties.
cards.explanation: The tiering runs the other way: weaker counterparties get lower MTAs, not higher ones.
cards.originalText: Tier the MTA by credit rating, with higher MTAs for lower‑rated counterparties.
cards.correction: Collateral agreements typically tier the minimum transfer amount by credit rating, with higher MTAs for higher-rated counterparties.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the features of a collateralization agreement.
cards.statement: Following best practice, collateral posting should be continuous for both parties.
cards.explanation: Margining is periodic, at least daily, to keep the operational workload under control. Continuous posting is not best practice.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the features of a collateralization agreement.
cards.statement: Variation margin is collateral that tracks the change in the mark-to-market of the position over time.
cards.explanation: Variation margin follows the MtM of the position.
cards.originalText: Variation margin is collateral that tracks the change in the MtM of the position over time.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the features of a collateralization agreement.
cards.statement: In a collateral agreement, the threshold and the minimum transfer amount are additive: exposure must exceed their sum before a call can be made.
cards.explanation: A call requires the amount above the threshold to exceed the MTA, so exposure must exceed the threshold plus the MTA.
cards.originalText: The threshold and the minimum transfer amount are additive: exposure must exceed their sum before a call can be made.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the features of a collateralization agreement.
cards.statement: Increasing the threshold in a collateral agreement increases the mitigation of exposure to counterparty default.
cards.explanation: A higher threshold leaves more exposure uncollateralised and so reduces mitigation. A zero threshold means full collateralisation.
cards.originalText: Increase the threshold
cards.correction: Increasing the threshold in a collateral agreement reduces the mitigation of exposure to counterparty default.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the features of a collateralization agreement.
cards.statement: Increasing the independent amount in a collateral agreement increases the mitigation of exposure to counterparty default.
cards.explanation: Initial margin adds overcollateralisation, which improves mitigation.
cards.originalText: Increase the independent amount

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the features of a collateralization agreement.
cards.statement: Decreasing the minimum transfer amount in a collateral agreement increases the mitigation of exposure to counterparty default.
cards.explanation: A smaller MTA lets smaller exposures be collateralised.
cards.originalText: Decrease the minimum transfer amount

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the features of a collateralization agreement.
cards.statement: Increasing the margin call frequency, for example from weekly to daily, increases the mitigation of exposure to counterparty default.
cards.explanation: More frequent calls reduce the unprotected exposure between calls.
cards.originalText: Increase the margin call frequency (e.g., from weekly to daily)

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the features of a collateralization agreement.
cards.statement: Higher initial margins protect against gap risk, the risk that a portfolio's value may gap substantially in a short period of time.
cards.explanation: Initial margin is an extra cushion that stays in place even when variation margin lags, so it is sized to absorb large sudden movements in value if the counterparty defaults.
cards.originalText: Higher initial margins

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the features of a collateralization agreement.
cards.statement: Higher thresholds protect against gap risk, the risk that a portfolio's value may gap substantially in a short period of time.
cards.explanation: A higher threshold increases the uncollateralised exposure below which no margin can be called, so it worsens gap risk.
cards.originalText: Higher thresholds

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the features of a collateralization agreement.
cards.statement: Higher minimum transfer amounts protect against gap risk, the risk that a portfolio's value may gap substantially in a short period of time.
cards.explanation: A higher MTA delays small transfers and adds to residual uncollateralised exposure, so it weakens protection.
cards.originalText: Higher minimum transfer amounts (MTA)

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the features of a collateralization agreement.
cards.statement: Given funding and capital costs and the shift toward central clearing and bilateral margin requirements, thresholds in collateral agreements are increasingly zero.
cards.explanation: Non-zero thresholds remain only for parties exempt from bilateral margin requirements, and central clearing requires full margining.
cards.originalText: More zero thresholds

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the features of a collateralization agreement.
cards.statement: Daily is the most common margin call frequency in OTC derivatives markets.
cards.explanation: Daily margin calls are the standard in most OTC derivatives markets. Intraday calls are mainly for repos and cleared products.
cards.originalText: Daily

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the features of a collateralization agreement.
cards.statement: Weekly is the most common margin call frequency in OTC derivatives markets.
cards.explanation: Weekly calls can be agreed with smaller or low-volatility counterparties, but daily calls are the norm.
cards.originalText: Weekly
cards.correction: Daily is the most common margin call frequency in OTC derivatives markets.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Differentiate between a two-way and one-way CSA agreement and describe how collateral parameters can be linked to credit quality.
cards.statement: When a downgrade trigger in a derivative contract is activated, the counterparty is required to post additional collateral, or the outstanding transactions may be terminated at market values.
cards.explanation: A downgrade trigger gives the protected party additional collateral, or the right to close out at market value, as soon as credit quality falls below the agreed level.
cards.originalText: The counterparty would be required to post additional collateral or potentially terminate outstanding transactions at market values.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Differentiate between a two-way and one-way CSA agreement and describe how collateral parameters can be linked to credit quality.
cards.statement: When a downgrade trigger in a derivative contract is activated, the counterparty is granted a grace period to improve its credit rating before any action is taken.
cards.explanation: A trigger takes effect immediately. A grace period would defeat its purpose of protecting against rapid credit deterioration.
cards.originalText: The counterparty would be granted a grace period to improve their credit rating before any action is taken.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Differentiate between a two-way and one-way CSA agreement and describe how collateral parameters can be linked to credit quality.
cards.statement: When a downgrade trigger in a derivative contract is activated, netting is suspended and the full gross value of all outstanding transactions becomes due immediately.
cards.explanation: Netting remains in force. A trigger does not suspend it, and any close-out is at the net market value.
cards.originalText: Netting will be suspended, and the full gross value of all outstanding transactions becomes due immediately.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Differentiate between a two-way and one-way CSA agreement and describe how collateral parameters can be linked to credit quality.
cards.statement: In a two-way collateral agreement, whichever party has a negative mark-to-market value on the portfolio posts collateral to the other, so the direction of posting can change as exposure changes.
cards.explanation: Two-way means either party may be the collateral provider, depending on which side of the net exposure it is on. If the portfolio value changes sign, the collateral flows reverse.
cards.originalText: Whichever party has a negative mark‑to‑market value on the portfolio posts collateral to the other, so the direction of posting can change as exposure changes.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Differentiate between a two-way and one-way CSA agreement and describe how collateral parameters can be linked to credit quality.
cards.statement: In a two-way collateral agreement, both parties must post collateral at all times, regardless of the sign of the mark-to-market value.
cards.explanation: Collateral covers only the net exposure of the receiving party. A party that is in-the-money on the portfolio is not required to post.
cards.originalText: Both parties must post collateral at all times, regardless of the sign of the mark‑to‑market value.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Differentiate between a two-way and one-way CSA agreement and describe how collateral parameters can be linked to credit quality.
cards.statement: In a two-way collateral agreement, only the party with the weaker credit rating ever posts collateral and the other party never does.
cards.explanation: That describes a one-way agreement, in which only one party ever posts. In a two-way agreement either party may post, depending on the sign of the net exposure.
cards.originalText: Only the party with the weaker credit rating ever posts collateral, and the other party never does.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Differentiate between a two-way and one-way CSA agreement and describe how collateral parameters can be linked to credit quality.
cards.statement: Either party to a collateral agreement may unilaterally change the collateral terms at any time if its counterparty's credit quality deteriorates.
cards.explanation: Collateral terms can be linked to credit quality only through pre-agreed provisions such as rating triggers. A signed agreement cannot be amended unilaterally.
cards.originalText: Either party may unilaterally change the collateral terms at any time if its counterparty’s credit quality deteriorates.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Differentiate between a two-way and one-way CSA agreement and describe how collateral parameters can be linked to credit quality.
cards.statement: A tiered threshold approach, in which thresholds are linked to counterparty credit ratings and lower-rated counterparties have lower thresholds, balances risk management with operational efficiency.
cards.explanation: The threshold is the exposure left uncollateralised, so it should reflect credit quality. Rating-linked thresholds minimise workload for strong counterparties while protecting against weak ones.
cards.originalText: The bank decides to adopt a tiered threshold approach, where threshold levels are linked to the credit ratings of counterparties, with lower‑rated counterparties having lower thresholds.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Differentiate between a two-way and one-way CSA agreement and describe how collateral parameters can be linked to credit quality.
cards.statement: Under a one-way CSA, the party that does not post collateral is likely to pay charges for the counterparty risk (CVA), funding (FVA), collateral terms (ColVA) and/or capital requirements (KVA) that it imposes on the other party.
cards.explanation: In a one-way CSA only one party posts, so the poster bears additional risk and costs. The non-posting party is expected to compensate it for the xVA it imposes.
cards.originalText: If they agree to a one‑way CSA, the non‑collateral posting party is likely to pay charges for the counterparty risk (CVA), funding (FVA), collateral terms (ColVA), and/or capital requirements (KVA) they impose on the other party

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Differentiate between a two-way and one-way CSA agreement and describe how collateral parameters can be linked to credit quality.
cards.statement: Credit support annexes are rare among derivative counterparties, so the most likely approach is that there is no CSA.
cards.explanation: CSAs are not rare: banks almost always trade under CSAs and other financial institutions often do.
cards.originalText: As CSAs are rare, the most likely approach is ”No CSA”

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Differentiate between a two-way and one-way CSA agreement and describe how collateral parameters can be linked to credit quality.
cards.statement: Under a two-way CSA, either party can unilaterally edit the CSA after it has been signed.
cards.explanation: A signed CSA is a contract and cannot be changed unilaterally. Amendments require the agreement of both parties.
cards.originalText: If they agree to a two‑way CSA, then either party can unilaterally edit the CSA subsequent to signing the CSA

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Differentiate between a two-way and one-way CSA agreement and describe how collateral parameters can be linked to credit quality.
cards.statement: When dealing with a hedge fund, a bank would most likely negotiate a one-way collateral agreement in the bank's favour, given the bank's stronger credit rating.
cards.explanation: One-way agreements are used when counterparties differ significantly in credit quality, size or risk. A bank is typically of much higher credit quality than a hedge fund, so only the hedge fund posts collateral.
cards.originalText: one‑way agreement in the bank’s favor given the bank’s stronger credit rating.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Differentiate between a two-way and one-way CSA agreement and describe how collateral parameters can be linked to credit quality.
cards.statement: When dealing with a hedge fund, a bank would most likely negotiate a two-way collateral agreement because of the small difference in credit quality between the two.
cards.explanation: Two-way agreements suit similar counterparties such as banks. A bank and a hedge fund have a large, not small, credit quality gap, which supports a one-way agreement.
cards.originalText: two‑way agreement given the relatively small difference in credit quality between the two entities.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization.
cards.statement: Collateralization of derivatives increases funding liquidity risk because collateral must be delivered on time, often within tight timescales.
cards.explanation: Collateral calls require liquid assets within short timescales, so counterparty risk is partly transformed into funding liquidity risk.
cards.originalText: It increases funding liquidity risk due to the need for timely payments, often within tight timescales.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization.
cards.statement: Collateralization of derivatives reduces operational risk by simplifying trade entry and settlement processes.
cards.explanation: Collateral management adds missed calls, failed deliveries and human error, so operational risk increases rather than decreases.
cards.originalText: It reduces operational risk by simplifying trade entry and settlement processes.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization.
cards.statement: Collateralization of derivatives eliminates market risk by ensuring an objective valuation of the underlying transactions.
cards.explanation: Residual market risk remains over the margin period of risk and within thresholds and minimum transfer amounts, so it is not eliminated.
cards.originalText: It eliminates market risk by ensuring an objective valuation of the underlying transactions.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization.
cards.statement: Adding a bilateral collateral arrangement to a derivatives contract that previously had no collateral reduces counterparty risk.
cards.explanation: Collateral lowers exposure to the counterparty's default. It transforms risk into operational, market and funding liquidity risks rather than removing it.
cards.originalText: Acme reduced counterparty risk

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization.
cards.statement: Adding a bilateral collateral arrangement to a derivatives contract reduces operational risk.
cards.explanation: Operational risk rises, because collateral handling creates more processes (calls, valuation, delivery, reconciliation) and more chances for error.
cards.originalText: Acme reduced operational risk

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization.
cards.statement: Inaccurate valuation of collateral, leading to inadequate collateral postings and disputes with counterparties, is an example of operational risk arising from collateralization.
cards.explanation: Operational risk from collateral comes from handling: valuation errors, missed calls, failed deliveries and computer or human error. Wrong valuations cause wrong call amounts and disputes.
cards.originalText: Operational risk emerges due to inaccurate valuation of collateral, leading to inadequate collateral postings and potential disputes with counterparties.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization.
cards.statement: Using diversified collateral mitigates operational risk by reducing exposure to any single asset's volatility.
cards.explanation: Diversification addresses market and concentration risk of the collateral, not process failures, which are what operational risk covers.
cards.originalText: Operational risk is mitigated through the use of diversified collateral, reducing the bank’s exposure to any single asset’s volatility.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization.
cards.statement: Operational risk is unaffected by collateralization practices, because it is concerned mainly with market fluctuations and credit risk management.
cards.explanation: Collateralization adds operational risk through missed calls, failed deliveries and errors. Operational risk concerns processes, people and systems, not market or credit risk.
cards.originalText: Operational risk is unaffected by collateralization practices, as it is primarily concerned with market fluctuations and credit risk management.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization.
cards.statement: A firm faces funding liquidity risk in collateralization when it must post additional high-quality liquid assets as collateral during market downturns, potentially leading to a liquidity shortfall.
cards.explanation: Margin calls rise in stress, just when liquid assets are hardest and most expensive to obtain, so calls can exceed available liquid assets.
cards.originalText: GFB faces funding liquidity risk when it has to post additional high‑quality liquid assets as collateral during market downturns, potentially leading to a liquidity shortfall.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization.
cards.statement: Using long-term, illiquid assets as collateral minimises funding liquidity risk by securing a firm's obligations for an extended period.
cards.explanation: Posting illiquid assets does not reduce liquidity risk. Eligible collateral is typically cash or high-quality securities, and illiquid assets worsen liquidity strain.
cards.originalText: The use of long‑term, illiquid assets as collateral by GFB minimizes funding liquidity risk by securing its obligations for an extended period.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization.
cards.statement: Market moves between the last collateral posting and the receipt of collateral after a default can leave exposure only partly covered, so some residual market risk remains under collateralization.
cards.explanation: Collateral is called and delivered only periodically, subject to the threshold and minimum transfer amount. Over the margin period of risk exposure can grow uncollateralised.
cards.originalText: Market moves between the last collateral posting and the receipt of collateral after default can leave exposure only partly covered, so some residual risk remains.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization.
cards.statement: Posting collateral eliminates all market risk because exposure is reset to zero at every valuation date.
cards.explanation: Exposure is not reset to zero continuously. The delay (margin period of risk), the threshold and the minimum transfer amount all leave residual market risk.
cards.originalText: Posting collateral eliminates all market risk because exposure is reset to zero at every valuation date.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization.
cards.statement: Market risk in a collateralised derivatives agreement arises only when the collateral is cash held in a different currency from the trade.
cards.explanation: A currency mismatch is one source of FX risk, but the market risk created by collateralization comes mainly from exposure moving over the margin period of risk and within thresholds and minimum transfer amounts.
cards.originalText: Market risk arises only when the collateral is cash held in a different currency from the trade.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization.
cards.statement: A bank that hedges uncollateralised client transactions with bilaterally collateralised trades faces an imbalance in collateral flows, because it must fund margin on the hedge without receiving offsetting margin on the client trade.
cards.explanation: When the client trade moves in the client's favour, the bank posts margin on the hedge but receives none on the client trade. This one-sided margin flow strains liquidity.
cards.originalText: Discrepancy between uncollateralized client transactions and bilaterally collateralized hedges.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization.
cards.statement: A company that pays fixed on a collateralised swap hedging its floating-rate debt faces funding liquidity risk when rates fall, because it must post variation margin immediately while the benefit of lower interest on its debt arrives only gradually.
cards.explanation: When rates fall the swap's mark-to-market turns negative for the fixed payer, who must deliver variation margin daily. The debt savings accrue slowly as coupons reset.
cards.originalText: Funding liquidity risk, because the swap has a negative MtM and Global must post liquid variation margin immediately, while the offsetting benefit (lower interest on its debt) arrives only gradually.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization.
cards.statement: Daily exchange of variation margin reduces operational risk by automatically eliminating valuation disputes and failed deliveries.
cards.explanation: Daily margining increases the operational burden (calls, delivery, valuation, reconciliation) and the chance of disputes and failures, rather than reducing them.
cards.originalText: Reduced operational risk, because daily margin automatically eliminates valuation disputes and failed deliveries.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization.
cards.statement: Minimum transfer amounts, thresholds and the margin period of risk leave exposure that can move before collateral is received, creating market risk.
cards.explanation: Between the last posting and the receipt of collateral, market moves can increase exposure. This residual, hard-to-hedge risk is market risk created by collateralization.
cards.originalText: Minimum transfer amounts, thresholds and the margin period of risk leave exposure that can move before collateral is received, creating market risk.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization.
cards.statement: Missed collateral calls, failed deliveries and human error create market risk.
cards.explanation: Process failures such as missed calls, failed deliveries and human error are operational risk, not market risk.
cards.originalText: Missed collateral calls, failed deliveries and human error create market risk.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization.
cards.statement: Price impact and transaction costs incurred when liquidating a large collateral position create operational risk.
cards.explanation: Price impact and liquidation costs are liquidity (liquidation) risk, not operational risk.
cards.originalText: Price impact and transaction costs when liquidating a large collateral position create operational risk.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization.
cards.statement: Difficulty in meeting frequent, large margin calls creates operational risk.
cards.explanation: The inability to fund margin calls is funding liquidity risk. Operational risk concerns errors and failures in processes.
cards.originalText: Difficulty in meeting frequent, large margin calls creates operational risk.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization.
cards.statement: Liquidation risk occurs when the amount of a security sold is large relative to its typical trading volume, which may drive down its price.
cards.explanation: Selling an amount large relative to normal volume can move the price and cause a substantial loss. Selling slowly instead exposes the holder to market volatility during liquidation.
cards.originalText: Liquidation risk occurs when the amount of a security sold is large relative to its typical trading volume, which may drive down its price.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization.
cards.statement: Liquidity risk in collateral agreements is eliminated entirely once an appropriate haircut is applied to the collateral.
cards.explanation: A haircut gives a buffer but does not remove price-impact losses that exceed the haircut.
cards.originalText: Liquidity risk is eliminated entirely once an appropriate haircut is applied to the collateral.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization.
cards.statement: Liquidation risk arises only if the issuer of the collateral security defaults, not from the size of the position sold.
cards.explanation: Issuer default is a separate risk. Liquidation risk is driven mainly by the size of the sale relative to market depth.
cards.originalText: Liquidation risk arises only if the issuer of the collateral security defaults, not from the size of the position sold.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain how market risk, operational risk, and liquidity risk (including funding liquidity risk) can arise through collateralization.
cards.statement: Liquidity risk occurs when there are potential pitfalls in the handling of collateral, including human error.
cards.explanation: Pitfalls in handling collateral, including human error, are operational risk. Liquidity risk concerns funding margin calls and the cost of selling assets.
cards.originalText: Liquidity risk occurs when there are potential pitfalls in the handling of collateral, including human error.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount.
cards.statement: A shorter remargining period decreases exposure to market volatility, because collateral is adjusted more frequently and the period during which exposure can rise uncollateralised is smaller.
cards.explanation: The margin period of risk creates exposure equal to the change in value that can occur before collateral is received. Shortening it reduces that change.
cards.originalText: It decreases exposure to market volatility because collateral is adjusted more frequently, shrinking the period during which exposure can rise uncollateralized.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount.
cards.statement: A shorter remargining period increases exposure to market volatility and counterparty risk.
cards.explanation: The relationship is reversed: a longer, not shorter, remargining period gives exposure more time to grow before collateral arrives.
cards.originalText: It increases exposure to market volatility and counterparty risk.
cards.correction: A longer remargining period increases exposure to market volatility and counterparty risk.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount.
cards.statement: The length of the remargining period has no significant impact on credit exposure.
cards.explanation: The margin period of risk is a primary driver of residual exposure under collateralization, especially in volatile markets.
cards.originalText: It has no significant impact on exposure.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount.
cards.statement: Lowering the threshold in a collateral agreement reduces credit risk, because collateral is called for smaller exposures.
cards.explanation: The threshold is exposure left uncollateralised by design, so the lower it is, the less exposure remains uncovered.
cards.originalText: Lowering the threshold reduces credit risk because collateral is called for smaller exposures.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount.
cards.statement: Increasing the threshold in a collateral agreement reduces credit risk because more collateral is posted.
cards.explanation: A higher threshold means less collateral is called, so more exposure stays uncollateralised and credit risk increases.
cards.originalText: Increasing the threshold reduces credit risk because more collateral is posted.
cards.correction: Increasing the threshold in a collateral agreement increases credit risk because less collateral is posted.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount.
cards.statement: The threshold in a collateral agreement has no significant impact on credit risk and only affects operational efficiency.
cards.explanation: The threshold directly determines the amount of exposure that is never collateralised, so it matters for credit risk as well as for operations.
cards.originalText: The threshold has no significant impact on credit risk; it only affects operational efficiency.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount.
cards.statement: A higher threshold in a collateral agreement reduces credit risk because it lowers the frequency of collateral calls.
cards.explanation: A higher threshold does reduce call frequency and administrative cost, but it increases, not decreases, credit risk because more exposure is uncollateralised.
cards.originalText: A higher threshold reduces credit risk because it lowers the frequency of collateral calls.
cards.correction: A higher threshold in a collateral agreement increases credit risk even though it lowers the frequency of collateral calls.

changes.from: reduces credit risk because it lowers
changes.to: increases credit risk even though it lowers

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount.
cards.statement: For risk assessment, the remargin period equals the legal margin call frequency, which is typically one day.
cards.explanation: The margin period of risk runs from the call to actual receipt and includes valuation, delivery, settlement and legal delays on top of the call frequency, so it is longer than the margin call frequency.
cards.originalText: For risk assessment, the remargin period will equal the legal margin call frequency, i.e. typically one day.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount.
cards.statement: If a position is strongly collateralized, the primary concerns are the length of the remargin period and the volatilities of the exposure and the collateral.
cards.explanation: With zero threshold and no initial margin, the residual risk comes from the margin period of risk and from the volatility of the exposure and of the collateral.
cards.originalText: If a position is strongly collateralized, the primary concerns are the length of the remargin period and the volatilities of the exposure and the collateral.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount.
cards.statement: Imperfect collateralization at a given date can arise from the terms of the collateral agreement (threshold, minimum transfer amount, rounding), which prevent the full amount from being called.
cards.explanation: Thresholds, minimum transfer amounts and rounding all prevent the full exposure from being called.
cards.originalText: Imperfect collateralization at a given date can arise from the terms of the collateral agreement (threshold, minimum transfer amount, rounding), which prevent calling the full amount.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount.
cards.statement: Exposure may increase between margin calls, and that portion of the exposure cannot be collateralized.
cards.explanation: Collateral is called only at discrete dates, so any exposure growth between calls remains uncollateralised until the next call and delivery.
cards.originalText: Exposure may increase between margin calls, and that portion cannot be collateralized.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount.
cards.statement: A lower collateral threshold implies that a larger portion of exposure is protected by collateral.
cards.explanation: The threshold is an amount of exposure that is never collateralised, so reducing it increases the share of exposure covered by collateral.
cards.originalText: A lower threshold implies that a larger portion of exposure is protected by collateral.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount.
cards.statement: A shorter margin period of risk implies that a smaller portion of exposure is protected by collateral.
cards.explanation: A shorter margin period of risk leaves less time for exposure to grow before collateral arrives, so more of the exposure is protected.
cards.originalText: A shorter margin period of risk implies that a smaller portion of exposure is protected by collateral.
cards.correction: A shorter margin period of risk implies that a larger portion of exposure is protected by collateral.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount.
cards.statement: A lower independent amount (initial margin) implies that a larger portion of exposure is protected by collateral.
cards.explanation: Lower initial margin means a smaller collateral cushion, so a smaller portion of exposure is protected.
cards.originalText: A lower independent amount (initial margin) implies that a larger portion of exposure is protected by collateral.
cards.correction: A lower independent amount (initial margin) implies that a smaller portion of exposure is protected by collateral.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount.
cards.statement: The protection from collateral specified in a CSA is uniform throughout the life of the exposure profile.
cards.explanation: Collateral is path-dependent, and the threshold and minimum transfer amount bind differently as exposure changes, so protection is not uniform over time.
cards.originalText: The protection from collateral specified in the CSA is uniform throughout the life of the exposure profile.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount.
cards.statement: A higher collateral threshold reduces the frequency of collateral exchanges and administrative cost but increases uncollateralised credit risk.
cards.explanation: A higher threshold means collateral is only called for exposure above it, so there are fewer calls but a larger permanently uncollateralised amount.
cards.originalText: A higher threshold reduces the frequency of collateral exchanges and administrative cost but increases uncollateralized credit risk.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount.
cards.statement: A longer remargining period reduces both operational burden and exposure to market value changes of the derivatives.
cards.explanation: A longer remargining period lengthens the margin period of risk and so increases exposure; the operational saving does not offset this.
cards.originalText: A longer remargining period reduces both operational burden and exposure to market value changes of the derivatives.
cards.correction: A longer remargining period reduces operational burden but increases exposure to market value changes of the derivatives.

changes.from: reduces both operational burden and exposure
changes.to: reduces operational burden but increases exposure

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount.
cards.statement: A lower minimum transfer amount increases the frequency of collateral movements, which reduces both exposure and transaction costs.
cards.explanation: More frequent collateral movements reduce exposure but raise operational and transaction costs.
cards.originalText: A lower minimum transfer amount increases the frequency of collateral movements, which reduces both exposure and transaction costs.
cards.correction: A lower minimum transfer amount increases the frequency of collateral movements, which reduces exposure but increases transaction costs.

changes.from: reduces both exposure and transaction costs
changes.to: reduces exposure but increases transaction costs

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount.
cards.statement: Shortening the remargining period and lowering the threshold and minimum transfer amount have no significant impact on exposure.
cards.explanation: The threshold, minimum transfer amount and margin period of risk are the main sources of residual exposure under collateralization, so changing them matters.
cards.originalText: Shortening the remargining period and lowering the threshold and minimum transfer amount have no significant impact on exposure.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount.
cards.statement: A larger independent amount (initial margin) posted by the counterparty increases the risk of a collateralised expected exposure profile.
cards.explanation: Initial margin held acts as a cushion against exposure and therefore reduces expected exposure, whereas the other terms each leave exposure uncollateralised.
cards.originalText: A larger independent amount (initial margin) posted by the counterparty
cards.correction: A larger independent amount (initial margin) posted by the counterparty reduces the risk of a collateralised expected exposure profile.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount.
cards.statement: A longer remargin period tends to increase the risk of the expected exposure profile of a collateralised position.
cards.explanation: A longer margin period of risk means exposure can grow for longer before collateral is received.
cards.originalText: A longer remargin period

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount.
cards.statement: A higher collateral threshold tends to increase the risk of the expected exposure profile of a collateralised position.
cards.explanation: The threshold is exposure that is never collateralised, so a higher threshold leaves more exposure uncovered.
cards.originalText: A higher threshold

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount.
cards.statement: A larger minimum transfer amount tends to increase the risk of the expected exposure profile of a collateralised position.
cards.explanation: Exposure below the minimum transfer amount is not called, so a larger minimum transfer amount means a larger uncollateralised gap.
cards.originalText: A larger minimum transfer amount

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount.
cards.statement: The annual review and renegotiation of the collateral threshold in the credit support annex is one of the time steps that make up the margin period of risk.
cards.explanation: The margin period of risk measures only the operational and legal delays between the margin call and the completed close-out and re-hedge. A periodic review of the threshold is not part of that chain.
cards.originalText: Annual review and renegotiation of the collateral threshold in the credit support annex

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the impact of collateralization on exposure and assess the risk associated with the remargining period, threshold, and minimum transfer amount.
cards.statement: The margin period of risk includes the time needed to value the exposure and collateral and to make the margin call.
cards.explanation: Valuation of exposure and collateral and issuing a valid margin call is the first time step of the margin period of risk.
cards.originalText: Valuation of the exposure and collateral, and the margin call

cards.subject: Credit Risk
